output.decision: Do not reallocate budget solely because Google brand search reports 5 ROAS versus TikTok prospecting at 2 ROAS. These activities serve different demand stages: brand search commonly captures existing intent, while prospecting may create demand that is credited elsewhere. Consider a controlled, bounded reallocation only after checking incremental performance, marginal returns, and measurement comparability.
next_steps: Verify both ROAS figures use the same attribution window, conversion definition, revenue basis, and treatment of returns/cancellations.
Review spend levels, impression share or budget limitation for brand search, and whether additional brand-search spend would buy incremental conversions rather than cannibalize organic/direct demand.
Compare marginal ROAS and contribution margin, not only 30-day average ROAS, for each channel.
Run a time-bounded budget test with predefined guardrails; evaluate total incremental revenue or profit, not platform-attributed ROAS alone.
Segment results by new versus returning customers and assess whether TikTok-assisted conversions later appear in branded search.
missing_inputs: Spend, revenue, conversion volume, and trend by channel during the 30-day period.
Attribution models/windows, conversion definitions, and whether reported ROAS includes returns, discounts, taxes, or shipping.
Contribution margins, customer-acquisition goals, and allowable CAC/ROAS thresholds.
Brand-search impression share, query mix, organic cannibalization indicators, and TikTok new-customer/assisted-conversion data.
assumptions: General ecommerce measurement guidance is used because no library evidence was supplied.
The reported ROAS values are platform or channel reported metrics and may not be directly comparable.
Google brand search and TikTok prospecting have materially different roles in the purchase journey.
